headline_marked: Australia [[tightens immigration policies]], causing anxiety for students
headline: Australia tightens immigration policies, causing anxiety for students
summary: New restrictions on visa hopping, family sponsorship, and tourist visas aim to reduce net migration to 245,000 by 2026-27.
details: The Australian government has introduced strict new immigration policies to combat housing shortages and rising living costs. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced the measures at the National Press Club in Canberra.

A key focus is ending 'visa hopping,' where international students switch to lower-quality courses just to extend their stay. Restrictions are also being placed on bringing family members, though PhD students and those already in the country will receive exemptions.

Tourist visas will now include a 'no further stay' condition, effectively preventing visitors from applying for other visas while in Australia. The government is also strengthening enforcement to ensure those with expired visas leave the country quickly.

Net migration is targeted to drop to 245,000 by the 2026-27 fiscal year and further to 225,000 in subsequent years. Priority will be given to skilled migrants in sectors with labor shortages, such as healthcare, construction, and agriculture.

The moves have sparked widespread protests from international students in major cities like Sydney, Melbourne, and Brisbane. Thousands of students skipped classes to demonstrate against the sudden policy shifts.
Bangladeshi students in Australia have expressed deep concern, stating that frequent rule changes and the ban on visa hopping create extreme uncertainty for their futures and financial investments.

headline_marked: [[Former RAB intelligence chief Ziaul Ahsan led 5 'golfing operations' killing 21]], witness testifies
headline: Former RAB intelligence chief Ziaul Ahsan led 5 'golfing operations' killing 21, witness testifies
summary: A former RAB officer testified that 21 abducted individuals were killed in five operations, with bodies dumped in rivers after gruesome methods, including being shot and having abdomens cut open.
details: A former deputy commander of RAB-8, Maj (retd) Sabbir Rahman Osmani, testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1, alleging that then RAB intelligence chief Lt Col Ziaul Ahsan led five operations resulting in the deaths of 21 abducted individuals. Osmani, the 13th prosecution witness, stated that bodies of some victims were later dumped in rivers.

Sabbir described a chilling pattern where victims were kept hooded and handcuffed before being killed. Operatives tied cement sacks to their legs and neck, pressed pillows against their heads, and shot them. Another individual then cut open their abdomens before the bodies were discarded into the river.

The river's depth was reportedly measured beforehand to prevent bodies from being traced. These operations were referred to as "golfing." According to Sabbir, Ziaul Ahsan justified these actions by stating, "They are harmful for the state. It is better to eliminate them. They have to be golfed this way," and reassured personnel that "the highest level of the state is aware of the incidents."

Sabbir also testified that Ziaul ordered the "elimination" of Alkas, whose boat was used in some operations, after Alkas allegedly disclosed operational information. Days later, Alkas's family reported him missing after he was summoned in Ziaul's name.

Ziaul Ahsan is currently facing trial for allegedly orchestrating the enforced disappearance and murder of 104 people between 2010 and 2013. Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that the witness's "horrific" testimony alone is sufficient to establish the charges against Ziaul.
